title: I Accidentally Became a government employee with a suspicious sword but the World Has Other Plans
synopsis: A royal archivist investigates a missing historical document and discovers that history itself has misplaced several chapters. The story unfolds in The Seven Provinces of Specific Laws, where magic obeys written clauses more strongly than spoken commands. The central problem is a missing royal relic that insists it was never missing. Kian Voss wants to collect evidence before anyone notices the plot, but every reasonable solution creates a new unreasonable obligation.
premise: A royal archivist investigates a missing historical document and discovers that history itself has misplaced several chapters.
authorNotes: I intended to write a dignified fantasy epic. The characters disagreed.

world.name: The Seven Provinces of Specific Laws
world.rule: Magic obeys written clauses more strongly than spoken commands.
world.oddity: Every province has a different definition of what counts as a dragon.
world.magic: Contract magic turns promises, receipts, and signatures into real spells.
world.threat: a missing royal relic that insists it was never missing

chapters.title: Apparently We Now Have To the Emergency Meeting — Kian Voss POV
chapters.arcTitle: The Problem With The Original Plan
paragraphs: CHAPTER 1 — Kian Voss POV
The Problem With The Original Plan had already produced two meetings, one argument, and a document nobody could legally throw away.
Kian Voss arrived at the capital registry intending to collect evidence before anyone notices the plot. The plan lasted until the first unexpected detail appeared.
A sealed document appears in the wrong person's hands.
Kian Voss knew, with the terrible certainty reserved for prophecies and overdue bills, that this moment mattered.
The important object was a invoice. It was not magical in the usual sense, which made it considerably more suspicious.
Kian Voss checked the obvious explanation first. It was wrong. They checked the ridiculous explanation next. It was unfortunately closer.
The world of The Seven Provinces of Specific Laws followed one inconvenient rule: Magic obeys written clauses more strongly than spoken commands.
The conversation became quieter when everyone realized that the newest clue had a date older than the kingdom itself.
Somewhere, history was preparing to make a poor decision.
A second person arrived carrying information about the suspicious invoice. Their explanation contradicted the first explanation in exactly the way a useful clue should.
Nobody agreed on what to do with the invoice. One person wanted to destroy it. Another wanted to file it. Kian Voss wanted to know why it had appeared here.
That question led to a small discovery: Kian Voss has a private connection to the missing relic.
The mystery remained open, although Kian Voss now had one useful fact: someone was treating the suspicious invoice as if it were a normal administrative matter.
Before leaving, Kian Voss made a decision that would matter later: they would not trust the next official document until they had read the footnotes.
For the first time that day, everyone agreed on something. This was probably going to get worse.
